Source. After the bitmap section of the attacker-controlled PIZ chunk, the decoder reads the next 32-bit field as `hufbytes`, the byte length of the Huffman-coded payload.

This chunk-level bounds check is present and succeeds on the staged witness, so the sub-buffer `[packed + nBytes, packed + nBytes + hufbytes)` is admitted as the Huffman input for `internal_huf_decompress()`.

The Huffman decoder materializes attacker-controlled header fields from the admitted sub-buffer: the symbol range `[im, iM]` and the encoded bit count `nBits` that govern fast-table initialization and later decode length.

The decoder advances `ptr` to the Huffman table bytes after the 20-byte header, derives the declared bitstream size from `nBits`, and passes the existing size check. `fasthuf_initialize()` is then entered with `*table == ptr` and `numBytes == nCompressed - hufInfoBlockSize`.
Fast table setup computes `topByte` as the end of the admitted table buffer and enforces a present exhaustion check only before reading the initial 6-bit `codeLen` for each symbol.

On the crashing iteration the guarded 6-bit read succeeds and yields `codeLen == LONG_ZEROCODE_RUN`, selecting the branch that must consume one additional 8-bit run-length value from the same input stream.

Root-cause step. After `codeLen` identifies `LONG_ZEROCODE_RUN`, vulnerable code immediately asks for the extra 8 run-length bits but does not repeat the `currByte >= topByte` truncation check that guarded the 6-bit read.

Sink. The 8-bit request from step 7 reaches `fasthuf_read_bits()` with too few buffered bits left, so the refill loop executes and dereferences `*currByte` even though `currByte` has already reached `topByte`, producing the saved one-byte heap-buffer-overflow read.

First project-side materialization of vulnerability-relevant attacker data on the reproduced path. The PIZ decoder reads the next 32-bit field from the packed chunk as the byte length of the Huffman-coded payload that will be handed to `internal_huf_decompress()`.
Root cause. After a `LONG_ZEROCODE_RUN` marker has been read, vulnerable code requests the extra 8-bit run length without first checking whether `currByte` has already reached `topByte`.

ASan sink. `fasthuf_read_bits()` refills its bit buffer by dereferencing `*currByte` even though `currByte` has already reached `topByte`, so the byte load lands exactly one byte past the packed chunk buffer.
